title: ZoneInfo validation must turn OSError from the tz lookup into a zoneinfo_str ValidationError
answers: ZoneInfo field raises IsADirectoryError instead of ValidationError
long timezone string gives 'File name too long' error in pydantic
which exceptions does the zoneinfo validator catch
body:
Symptom: validating a `ZoneInfo` field with a string such as 'America' (which names a tzdata directory) or a very long string (e.g. 300 chars) raised a raw OSError (IsADirectoryError / filename too long) instead of a pydantic ValidationError.
Root cause: pydantic/_internal/_validators.py:validate_str_is_valid_iana_tz calls `ZoneInfo(value)`, which looks the key up on the filesystem. The except clause only caught ZoneInfoNotFoundError, ValueError and TypeError, so filesystem errors escaped.
Fix pattern: add OSError to the caught exceptions and re-raise as `PydanticCustomError('zoneinfo_str', 'invalid timezone: {value}', {'value': value})`. Any validator that wraps a stdlib constructor doing I/O on user input should catch OSError as well as the documented lookup errors.
Constraints: the error type ('zoneinfo_str'), message and ctx stay the same for all invalid inputs, and tests assert them exactly. ZoneInfo instances are passed through before the try block. Regression tests are in tests/types/test_zoneinfo.py:test_zoneinfo_os_error_is_validation_error.
applies: Validation of zoneinfo.ZoneInfo fields in pydantic/_internal/_validators.py
